what_is_in_here: One entry per CONFIGURATION field: something that changes what this deployment is, and that persists. Purely operational CLI flags are deliberately excluded, because they select an action rather than configure anything: --dry-run, --json, --limit, --follow, --scope, --severity, --source/--backup-set filters, --note, --content, --days, --medium, --acknowledge, --acknowledge-repoint, --acknowledge-host-key-change, --acknowledge-medium-disclosure, --release, --run, --inherit, --candidate, --stdin, --policy-file and --tier/--tier-medium as a preview override. Where such a flag is the only way to write a persistent field (--no-verify writing connection_unverified, --policy-file and --tier writing a retention chain) it is listed on that field instead.
known_asymmetries: storage_mediums[].path (a local_volume's directory) is configurable in the web UI through the manifest-driven destination wizard and has NO CLI flag at all: `medium add`/`medium edit` parse --type, --region, --endpoint, --bucket, --prefix, --storage-class, --upload-verification and the four credential spellings, and nothing else. The gap is the CLI's, not the UI's.

poll_interval is configurable in the web UI, at two scopes, and has no CLI flag at either (#845): Settings > Service behaviour writes the deployment-wide default, and a backup set's own Edit form writes or clears its override. The gap is the CLI's, not the UI's.

fields.description: EPIC K's production gate (#789): whether this deployment may run the incremental (kopia) backup engine at all. Defaults to FALSE, and an absent incremental_engine block is disabled. BACKUPD_INCREMENTAL_ENGINE overrides the file in BOTH directions (1|true|yes|on enables, 0|false|no|off disables, unset or empty defers to the file), and an unparseable value is refused at Validate rather than read as off. Resolved by config.IncrementalEngineEnabled() and nowhere else. With it off, creating or updating an engine: kopia set, that set's snapshot cycle, verification, maintenance, snapshot restore and the repository probes all refuse with config.ErrIncrementalEngineDisabled (409 INCREMENTAL_ENGINE_DISABLED, CLI exit 1); LOADING a configuration that declares kopia sets is deliberately NOT gated, so turning it off never stops a daemon whose artifact sets still have to run. Artifact backup sets are unaffected in either position. See docs/incremental-engine.md.

ui.recommendation: File-only on purpose: a release gate an operator can flip from the browser is one that gets flipped without the runbook beside it.

fields.default: derived from LISTEN_ADDR, with a wildcard bind rewritten to 127.0.0.1
fields.description: What the UI host's own container HEALTHCHECK GETs, since distroless has no shell, curl or wget.

ui.recommendation: file-only: consumed by the container runtime's HEALTHCHECK, not by an operator

fields.description: The FR-23 structured-log level every service surface and `backupd daemon` read from the environment, so the one engine an operator can run headless is not the one they cannot turn up.

ui.recommendation: file-only: read once from the process environment at startup; there is no reload path for it

fields.default: "" (no route: writes beside a serving engine are refused)
fields.description: Where the CLI on this host finds the serving engine, so a configuration write can be handed to it instead of refused. Deliberately not a flag.

ui.recommendation: file-only: it configures the CLI's route to the engine, on the host running the CLI; it is not a property of the deployment the UI edits

fields.description: Administrator username the CLI presents to the engine's API, held in memory for one invocation and written nowhere.

ui.recommendation: file-only: a credential for the CLI's own route; not a flag, because a password on a command line is in every process listing on the host

fields.description: Administrator password the CLI presents to the engine's API.

ui.recommendation: file-only: a credential for the CLI's own route, deliberately env-only
